item.text:
**8B.7 Assessment:** Mixed, leaning positive on the short-run macro and service-delivery record, but only partially positive on broader welfare. Growth, poverty, health coverage, and social-program targeting moved in the ruler’s stated direction; job quality, learning, and security/accountability in Papua lagged or worsened.

**Positive / on-track**
- [Macro Poverty Outlook for Indonesia: October 2024 Datasheet](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099026110152411280) - World Bank, 2024-10-02. Claim: Indonesia was growing at about 5% and poverty fell from 17.5% in 2023 to 15.8% in 2024, which is directionally consistent with Jokowi’s development/prosperity narrative, though job creation still lagged. IDs: `8B.7`, also `8B.1`, `8B.2`.
- [Indonesia: 2024 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Indonesia](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/08/07/indonesia-2024-article-iv-consultation-press-release-staff-report-and-statement-by-the-553165) - IMF, 2024-08-07. Claim: Growth stayed strong despite external headwinds, inflation remained in target, and the financial sector was resilient, so core macro outcomes broadly tracked the administration’s stability-oriented goals. IDs: `8B.7`, also `8B.2`, `8B.5`.
- [Does Indonesia’s National Health Insurance Scheme mobile phone application, Mobile JKN, support health financing?](https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789240100893) - World Health Organization, 2024-12-06. Claim: JKN/UHC goals were translated into observable improvements like easier registration, better informal-sector contributions, and lower administrative costs; health access and financial protection moved in the claimed direction. IDs: `8B.7`, also `8B.4`, `8B.6`.
- [Bappenas perkuat dukungan untuk anak-anak dan keluarga rentan](https://www.unicef.org/indonesia/id/press-releases/bappenas-perkuat-dukungan-untuk-anak-anak-dan-keluarga-rentan) - UNICEF Indonesia, 2024-04-25. Claim: Regsosek improved targeting, delivery, accountability, and transparency in social assistance, which suggests real progress toward better welfare delivery rather than slogan-only policy. IDs: `8B.7`, also `8B.4`, `8B.6`.
- [Blueprint: Get children back to school in Indonesia](https://www.unicef.org/indonesia/stories/blueprint-get-children-back-school-indonesia) - UNICEF Indonesia, 2024-08-23. Claim: The government-led back-to-school push returned nearly 37,000 children to learning and helped prevent about 149,000 dropouts since 2021, so one desired education outcome did move in the right direction. IDs: `8B.7`, also `8B.6`.

**Mixed / lagging / negative**
- [Indonesia - Learning Poverty Brief 2024](https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099082924151529593) - World Bank/UNESCO, 2024-04-01. Claim: Learning poverty remained a major drag on human capital and poverty reduction, so a key long-lag outcome did not clearly improve enough to validate the broader development story. IDs: `8B.7`, also `8B.6`.
- [Indonesia's dwindling middle class seen dimming economic outlook](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/indonesias-dwindling-middle-class-seen-dimming-economic-outlook-3610865) - Reuters, 2024-09-11. Claim: Layoffs and fewer job opportunities pushed many working- and middle-class Indonesians backward, which undercuts a clean reading that growth was translating into broadly improved household welfare. IDs: `8B.7`.
- [Indonesia Growth and Jobs Report Running Faster, for Longer](https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/indonesia/publication/indonesia-growth-and-jobs-report-running-faster-for-longer-structural-transformation-productivity-and-good-jobs) - World Bank, 2024. Claim: The economy made real gains over time, but job creation remained skewed toward lower-value activities and structural barriers kept productivity and good-job creation below the level implied by Jokowi’s development aims. IDs: `8B.7`, also `8B.2`, `8B.4`.
- [If It’s Not Racism, What Is It? Discrimination and Other Abuses Against Papuans in Indonesia](https://www.hrw.org/report/2024/09/18/if-it-s-not-racism-what-is-it/discrimination-and-other-abuses-against-papuans-in) - Human Rights Watch, 2024-09-18. Claim: Severe abuses and weak accountability in Papua mean protection and equal treatment outcomes moved in the wrong direction for a major vulnerable group, even if the center-right macro story improved. IDs: `8B.7`, also `8B.5`, `8B.6`.
- [Analysis: A decade of Jokowi’s Indonesia democracy icon leaves illiberal legacy, critics say](https://theprint.in/world/analysis-a-decade-of-jokowi-indonesias-democracy-icon-leaves-illiberal-legacy-critics-say/2310394/) - Reuters via ThePrint, 2024-10-14. Claim: Reuters’ end-of-term reading is that strong growth and infrastructure were real, but patronage, dynastic politics, and weaker institutional integrity mean the outcome mix was materially less clean than Jokowi’s pro-development claims implied. IDs: `8B.7`, also `8B.5`, `8B.6`.

**Search gap**
- I did not find a single 2024 document that scores Jokowi’s full claimed agenda end-to-end against outcomes. The evidence is sectoral, and the strongest short-run positives are macro stability, poverty reduction, health access, and targeted social delivery. The clearest lagging areas are job quality, learning outcomes, and Papuan safety/accountability.
